# CoreData

**Symbols:** 80.0% of Apple's iOS API (1099 of 1374, exact) · **Rows:** 22: 20 ✅ 1 🟡 1 ❌ · **iOS:** 3.0+

**Area:** [Data & persistence](../COVERAGE.md#data) · **Apple:** [CoreData](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/coredata) · **Issues:** [`area:data`](https://github.com/kolabs-dev/isim/issues?q=is%3Aissue+is%3Aopen+label%3Aarea%3Adata)

## How isim implements it

- **Adapted:** isim's own Objective-C engine (`isim/frameworks/CoreData`) on the host's SQLite (passthrough `libsqlite3`), with isim's own compiled model format.
- Guide: [COREDATA.md](../COREDATA.md).

## API

| API / feature | Status | iOS | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Core Data: stack (`NSPersistentContainer`, `NSPersistentStoreCoordinator`, `NSPersistentStoreDescription`) | ✅ | ≤17 | isim's Objective-C `CoreData` framework (+ Swift overlay). Container finds `<name>.momd` in the main bundle; SQLite store in Library/Application Support/`<name>`.sqlite; `/dev/null` URL or `NSInMemoryStoreType` = in-memory. Store layout is isim's own (see docs/COREDATA.md). Tested: CoreDataTest, HelloCoreData |
| Core Data: models (`NSManagedObjectModel`, `NSEntityDescription`, attributes, relationships, inheritance) | ✅ | ≤17 | Built in code or loaded from isim-compiled models. All attribute types incl. UUID, URI, Date, Binary, Decimal (as NSNumber/REAL), Transformable (value transformer data); to-one/to-many/ordered/many-to-many with inverses; fetch request templates, fetched properties, configurations. Tested: CoreDataTest |
| Core Data: `.xcdatamodeld` in Xcode projects + codegen | ✅ | ≤17 | `isim build` compiles `.xcdatamodeld`/`.xcdatamodel` (versions, `.xccurrentversion`) to `<Name>.momd` in **isim's own model format** (XML plists; not Apple's binary .mom) and generates the Swift that Xcode's Class Definition / Category codegen makes (`@NSManaged` properties, `fetchRequest()`, to-many accessors). Decimal attributes generate `NSNumber?` (Xcode: `NSDecimalNumber?`). Tested: CoreDataTest, HelloCoreData |
| Core Data: `NSManagedObject` (`@NSManaged` accessors, faults, KVC/KVO, `changedValues`, validation) | ✅ | ≤17 | Dynamic accessors via `+resolveInstanceMethod:` typed from the property's declared type (scalars, objects, `add<Key>Object:` & co., ordered accessors, `primitive<Key>`); `ObservableObject` + `Identifiable`; lazy faults (`object(with:)`, to-many loaded on first access); validation: mandatory, min/max, regex, validation predicates, `validate<Key>:error:`, relationship counts, deny. Tested: CoreDataTest |
| Core Data: `NSManagedObjectContext` (insert/delete/save/rollback/reset/refresh, delete rules, notifications) | ✅ | ≤17 | Cascade/nullify/deny/no-action; `ObjectsDidChange` (end of event / `processPendingChanges`), `WillSave`/`DidSave`; `perform`/`performAndWait` (+ async `perform`, `performBackgroundTask`), main/private queues; parent/child contexts; `automaticallyMergesChangesFromParent` (children and sibling root contexts); `mergeChanges(fromContextDidSave:)`, `mergeChanges(fromRemoteContextSave:into:)`; permanent IDs + `URIRepresentation`. Tested: CoreDataTest |
| Core Data: merge policies (`NSMergePolicy` with `resolve(mergeConflicts:)`, `resolve(optimisticLockingVersionConflicts:)`, `resolve(constraintConflicts:)`; `NSMergeConflict`, `NSConstraintConflict`) | ✅ | ≤17 | Optimistic locking per row; uniqueness constraints are checked on inserts. A save builds `NSMergeConflict`s (versions; persisted, cached and object snapshots) and `NSConstraintConflict`s (constraint, values, database object and snapshot) and hands them to the context's merge policy: the built-in policies resolve them per object (error: the save fails with them in `conflictList`; object trump, overwrite, store trump, rollback; property-level merge simplified), and a subclass overrides the resolve methods (a constraint conflict it leaves unmerged must no longer collide). Adapted: conflicts between objects inserted in the same save are not detected. Tested: error, object/store trump, overwrite, rollback, uniqueness (CoreDataTest), `NSMergeConflict` / `NSConstraintConflict` and two `NSMergePolicy` subclasses (CoreDataTest, ClassesTests.swift) |
| Core Data: `NSAsynchronousFetchRequest`, `NSAsynchronousFetchResult`, `NSPersistentStoreAsynchronousResult` | ✅ | ≤17 | adapted: `execute(_:)` returns the result at once; the fetch runs in a `perform` block on the context's queue and the completion block is called there; `progress` (a child of the current progress) finishes with it; `cancel()` before it runs keeps it from running and from calling the block. Tested: CoreDataTest, HelloCoreData (tests/ui/test_coredata.py) |
| Core Data: query generations (`NSQueryGenerationToken` with `.current`, `queryGenerationToken`, `setQueryGenerationFrom(_:)`) | ✅ | ≤17 | adapted: a token is an SQLite read transaction (WAL) on its own connection per store, kept while the token lives; a pinned context's fetches, counts and faults read through it, other contexts can pin to the same token, and saving, merging or resetting the context moves it to a new snapshot of the current data. Only root contexts pin (child contexts read through their parent); in-memory stores refuse. Tested: CoreDataTest |
| Core Data: `NSFetchRequest` (predicates, sorting, limits, result types) | ✅ | ≤17 | Comparisons, BEGINSWITH/ENDSWITH/CONTAINS/LIKE (`[c]` for ASCII), IN, BETWEEN, AND/OR/NOT, `nil`, to-one/SELF equality run as SQL; anything else (key paths across relationships, `@count`, ANY, custom selectors) is evaluated in memory; pending changes (inserted/updated/deleted) always included. Managed objects, object IDs, dictionaries (`propertiesToFetch`, `NSExpressionDescription` aggregates, group by), counts; `count(for:)`; `execute()` in perform blocks. `fetchBatchSize`/prefetching accepted, everything is fetched at once. Tested: CoreDataTest |
| Core Data: `NSBatchDeleteRequest` / `NSBatchUpdateRequest` / `NSBatchInsertRequest` | ✅ | ≤17 | Run directly in SQLite (batch delete does not run object delete-rule callbacks; dangling to-one keys and join rows are cleared); object-ID results merge with `mergeChanges(fromRemoteContextSave:into:)`. Batch insert supports dictionaries and dictionary/managed-object handlers. Tested: CoreDataTest |
| Core Data: `NSFetchedResultsController` | ✅ | ≤17 | Sections by key path, index titles, `object(at:)`/`indexPath(forObject:)`; delegate insert/delete/move/update + section changes, or `controller(_:didChangeContentWith:)` with an `NSDiffableDataSourceSnapshotReference` that bridges to `NSDiffableDataSourceSnapshot<String, NSManagedObjectID>`. No cache. Tested: CoreDataTest |
| Core Data: SwiftUI (`@FetchRequest`, `FetchedResults`, `@SectionedFetchRequest`, `\.managedObjectContext`) | ✅ | ≤17 | Re-fetches on context changes (saves, merges) with the request's animation; `nsPredicate`/`nsSortDescriptors` settable; Swift `SortDescriptor`s sort in memory. Tested: HelloCoreData |
| Core Data: migration (`NSMappingModel`, `NSEntityMapping` and `NSEntityMappingType`, `NSPropertyMapping`, `NSEntityMigrationPolicy`, `NSMigrationManager` with its source / destination contexts and instance associations, the `NSMigration…Key` variables) | ✅ | ≤17 | Automatic lightweight migration supports added entities/attributes/relationships and renaming identifiers. `NSMigrationManager.migrateStore…` runs Apple's pipeline over the mapping's entity mappings: each mapping's `NSEntityMigrationPolicy` (or the subclass named by `entityMigrationPolicyClassName`) creates the destination instances (attribute mappings' value expressions over `$source`), then their relationships (to the destination instances of the related source objects, or relationship mappings' expressions), then validates; the destination is saved, and migrating in place goes through a temporary file. `inferredMappingModel` builds copy / transform / add / remove mappings from names and renaming identifiers. Adapted: compiled mapping models (`.cdm`, `init(contentsOf:)`) are not read, and `sourceExpression` is not evaluated (every source instance is migrated). Tested: CoreDataTest (a policy subclass, relationships, in place) |
| Core Data: staged migration (`NSStagedMigrationManager`, `NSCustomMigrationStage` with `willMigrateHandler` / `didMigrateHandler`, `NSLightweightMigrationStage`, `NSManagedObjectModelReference`, `NSPersistentStoreStagedMigrationManagerOptionKey`, `NSManagedObjectModel.versionChecksum`) | ✅ | 17.0 | adapted: when the store opens, the custom stages from the store's model on run in order: `willMigrateHandler` with `container` on the stage's current model, then the store moves to the next model (isim's lightweight migration) and `didMigrateHandler` runs on it; lightweight stages are isim's automatic schema migration when the store opens with the final model. Tested: CoreDataTest |
| Core Data: persistent history, derived attributes, undo | 🟡 | ≤17 | With `NSPersistentHistoryTrackingKey`, every save records its transaction (author, context name, timestamp, `bundleID`, `processID`) and changes (object, type, `updatedProperties`) in the store's file (`ATRANSACTION`, `ACHANGE`), so history survives relaunches and is shared by every process that opens the store; history requests filter after tokens/dates/transactions and by their `fetchRequest`, with every result type, and delete history; derived expressions are evaluated before save; scalar, to-one and to-many mutations register with `undoManager`. Not yet: `tombstone` values. Tested: CoreDataTest, and HelloCoreData across three launches (tests/ui/test_coredata.py) |
| Core Data: `NSDerivedAttributeDescription`, `NSCompositeAttributeDescription` (iOS 17) | ✅ | ≤17 | adapted: a derived attribute's `derivationExpression` is evaluated in memory when an inserted or updated object is saved (Apple's store computes it in SQL). A composite attribute's value is a dictionary of its `elements`, stored as one binary-plist column (UUIDs and URLs as strings); predicates on its elements (`location.latitude < 0`) are evaluated in memory. `momc` compiles Xcode 15's `attributeType="Composite"` with its `<composite>` (codegen: `[String: Any]?`). Tested: CoreDataTest |
| Core Data: fetch indexes (`NSFetchIndexDescription`, `NSFetchIndexElementDescription`, `NSFetchIndexElementType`, `NSEntityDescription.indexes`) | ✅ | ≤17 | adapted: each index is an SQLite index on the entity's table (`Z_<ENTITY>_<NAME>`, ascending or descending columns), created whenever a store opens; partial when `partialIndexPredicate` translates to SQL; R-tree elements are ordinary indexes. `momc` compiles an `.xcdatamodel`'s `<fetchIndex>`. Tested: CoreDataTest (the SQLite schema, and TestModel's compiled index) |
| Core Data: `NSIncrementalStore`, `NSIncrementalStoreNode`, `NSSaveChangesRequest`, `registerStoreClass(_:forStoreType:)`, `registeredStoreTypes` | ✅ | ≤17 | An app's store class is added like any store type (its `loadMetadata()` sets the metadata; the store's identifier is its `NSStoreUUIDKey`). Contexts fetch through `execute(_:with:)` (the request with its entity; the store filters and sorts, unsaved changes are merged in), fire faults with `newValuesForObject(with:with:)`, load to-many (and missing to-one) relationships with `newValue(forRelationship:forObjectWith:with:)`, get IDs from `obtainPermanentIDs(for:)` and save with an `NSSaveChangesRequest`; object IDs carry the store's reference objects (in their URIs too), and contexts report the IDs they register and, on reset, unregister. Adapted: no optimistic locking (the store's business). Tested: CoreDataTest (a dictionary-backed store) |
| Core Data: `NSCoreDataCoreSpotlightDelegate` (`init(forStoreWith:coordinator:)`, `startSpotlightIndexing` / `stopSpotlightIndexing`, `attributeSet(for:)`, `domainIdentifier`, `indexName`, `deleteSpotlightIndex`, the reindex callbacks, `NSCoreDataCoreSpotlightDelegateIndexDidUpdate`), `isIndexedBySpotlight` | ✅ | ≤17 | adapted: indexes the attributes marked `isIndexedBySpotlight` (`spotlightIndexingEnabled` in an `.xcdatamodel`) into isim's CoreSpotlight when indexing starts and after every save on the coordinator (persistent history is not needed), so the home screen's Spotlight finds them; items are identified by the object's URI, in the store's domain. The default attribute set's title is `coreSpotlightDisplayNameExpression`'s value or the first indexed string, the rest its description and keywords; subclasses override `attributeSet(for:)`. CoreData loads CoreSpotlight at run time (the Swift overlay links it). Tested: CoreDataTest, HelloCoreData (tests/ui/test_coredata.py, the home screen's Spotlight) |
| Core Data: `NSPersistentStoreRemoteChange` (`NSPersistentStoreRemoteChangeNotificationPostOptionKey`, `NSPersistentStoreURLKey`, `NSPersistentHistoryTokenKey`) | ✅ | ≤17 | adapted: every write to a store file (saves, batch requests) posts a Darwin notification named after the file; a store with the option on posts `NSPersistentStoreRemoteChange` (object: its coordinator; on a background queue) for writes from any coordinator or process, with the store's UUID and URL and, with persistent history, the newest transaction's token. Tested: CoreDataTest (another coordinator's write), HelloCoreData |
| Core Data: `NSPersistentCloudKitContainer`, `NSPersistentCloudKitContainerOptions`, `cloudKitContainerOptions` | ✅ | ≤17 | adapted: an `NSPersistentContainer` subclass whose store stays on the device — **local, no iCloud mirroring**; options are remembered, `initializeCloudKitSchema` logs, record decisions succeed, and setup/export `eventChangedNotification` events bracket loads/saves. Tested: HelloCloudKit |
| Types not yet in isim (iOS 17 and earlier) | ❌ | ≤17 | not implemented, found by the 2026-10 sweep: `NSAtomicStore`, `NSAtomicStoreCacheNode` (2 types; with their members under "Not yet in isim") |
